title: Generic sections of finite schemes extend uniquely over normal integral bases
statement:
Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose local rings are normal domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $\eta$ be its generic point, put $K=\mathcal O_{S,\eta}=k(S)$ [def-sc-function-field], and let $j:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ be the generic-point morphism. Let $f:X\to S$ be any finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Restriction along $j$ is a bijection
$$\{s:S\to X\mid f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_S\}\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \{a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X\mid f\circ a=j\}.$$
Thus every prescribed generic section of $f$ extends to exactly one section over $S$. No reducedness, normality, integrality or flatness assumption on $X$, and no Noetherian or finite-type-over-a-field assumption on $S$, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AB1 (lemma-finite-birational-over-normal), applied to the reduced closure of a prescribed generic section; affine uniqueness by injection into the function field. Agent general finite-scheme formulation of the normal-base argument in de Jong 1997 section 3.8, returned proof steps 7--8.

proof.text: For each nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, finite affineness gives $X_U=f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite as an $A$-module. The generic point belongs to $U$, and its germ map $i_U:A\hookrightarrow K$ identifies $K$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Every localization $A_{\mathfrak m}$ at a maximal ideal is isomorphic to the corresponding local ring of $S$, hence is a normal domain by hypothesis. The local criterion for normal domains therefore makes $A$ integrally closed in $K$. Nonempty affine opens cover $S$.

source.place: Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local, (3) implies (1); Schemes Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves; Morphisms Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, affine normality argument

proof.text: Fix a prescribed $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ above $j$. Over each $U$ of step 1 it factors through $X_U$ and corresponds to a ring map $\phi_U:B\to K$ whose composite with $A\to B$ is $i_U$. For $b\in B$, finite integrality gives $b^n+c_{n-1}b^{n-1}+\cdots+c_0=0$ with $c_r\in A$. Applying $\phi_U$ gives $\phi_U(b)^n+i_U(c_{n-1})\phi_U(b)^{n-1}+\cdots+i_U(c_0)=0$. Thus $\phi_U(b)$ lies in $i_U(A)$ by normality. Define $\psi_U(b)$ to be its unique preimage in $A$. Applying the injective $i_U$ to the equations for sums, products, zero and one proves that $\psi_U:B\to A$ is a ring map; it is an $A$-algebra map because $i_U\psi_U$ is the identity on the image of $A$ in $B$. Consequently $s_U=\operatorname{Spec}(\psi_U):U\to X_U$ is a section restricting to $a$ at $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, monic-equation argument, adapted directly to the image of a generic-section map; Algebra Tag 00GK, lemma-finite-is-integral

proof.text: For any nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq S$, two sections over $W$ with the same generic restriction give maps $\theta_1,\theta_2:\Gamma(X_W,\mathcal O)\to C$. Their composites with the injective germ map $C\hookrightarrow K$ agree, since they are the ring maps of that same generic morphism. Hence $\theta_1=\theta_2$ elementwise, and affine contravariant functoriality gives equality of the sections. This proves local uniqueness without any assumption on the ring of $X_W$.

source.place: Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal, injective affine coordinate maps; Schemes Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine

proof.text: On $U\cap V$ cover by nonempty affine opens $W\subseteq U\cap V$. Each contains $\eta$. The restrictions $s_U|_W$ and $s_V|_W$ are sections over $W$ with generic restriction $a$, so step 3 makes them equal. Morphism gluing and its uniqueness clause give equality on $U\cap V$, including the vacuous empty case, and then glue all $s_U:U\to X$ to $s:S\to X$. Since $f\circ s$ restricts to the identity on every $U$, the same uniqueness clause gives $f\circ s=\mathrm{id}_S$. Its generic restriction is $a$, as may be checked on any one nonempty affine $U$.

source.place: Tags 04TN, lemma-glue-maps, and 00AN, lemma-mapping-property-glue; scheme morphism gluing as in Schemes Tag 01JA, section-glueing-schemes

proof.text: If two global sections have the same generic restriction, step 3 identifies them on every nonempty affine open of $S$; uniqueness of morphism gluing identifies them globally. Restriction is therefore injective, and step 4 proves it surjective. Composition with $j$ takes a section to a morphism above $j$ by associativity, so these are exactly the two sets in the statement. If the generic-section set is empty, the global-section set is empty too, and the same bijectivity assertion holds.
